description: The bar chart titled “Factual Errors” compares the number of factual errors across four question-answering datasets — HotpotQA, 2WikiMQA, MuSiQue, and IIRC — under three different QA methods: NoR QA (orange with grid pattern), OneR QA (red with dot pattern), and IRCOT QA (blue with diagonal stripe pattern), as evaluated in the paper “Interleaving Retrieval with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Knowledge-Intensive Multi-Step Questions.” The horizontal axis lists the four datasets, while the vertical axis represents the count of factual errors, ranging from 0 to 40 in increments of 5. For HotpotQA, NoR QA has 15 errors, OneR QA has 10, and IRCOT QA has 5. For 2WikiMQA, NoR QA has 29 errors, OneR QA has 23, and IRCOT QA has 14. For MuSiQue, NoR QA has 28 errors, OneR QA has 27, and IRCOT QA has 23. For IIRC, NoR QA has 15 errors, OneR QA has 14, and IRCOT QA has 11. Across all datasets, IRCOT QA consistently shows the lowest number of factual errors, followed by OneR QA, and then NoR QA, indicating improved factual accuracy with the interleaved retrieval and chain-of-thought approach. The bars are grouped by dataset, with each group containing three adjacent bars corresponding to the three methods, and the values are explicitly labeled atop each bar.
